copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. South Africa v Korea Republic in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Thursday, and the model and the market disagree on the Korea Republic side by +16.1pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Korea Republic 150 points higher than the other side (South Africa 1620, Korea Republic 1770). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: South Africa to win at 23%, the draw at 21%, and Korea Republic to win at 56%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Korea Republic sits at 56% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: South Africa to win at 30%, the draw at 29%, and Korea Republic to win at 40%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Korea Republic side — 40% on the market, 56% on the engine, a +16.1pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Korea Republic side that lower bound is 47% — +7.7pp clear of the market's 40%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Korea Republic side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +16.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Korea Republic look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 56% vs market 40% — a +16.1pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: South Africa v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
